report.summary: Established and repaired one implementation defect in generated/hello-world.mjs, the only file in write scope. Before the edit, the admitted observation and my own run agreed: `node generated/hello-world.mjs` exited 0 but printed "Hello world!\n" (13 bytes, missing the comma). Because of that, `node --test test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs` exited 1 with pass 0 and fail 2. I changed the single line from console.log("Hello world!") to console.log("Hello, world!"). I then ran two local checks. (1) The direct CLI exited 0, stderr was empty, and stdout was 14 bytes matching printf 'Hello, world!\n' byte for byte. (2) My first run of the planned test command used my host's environment, which carries NODE_TEST_CONTEXT=child-v8. Node warned that run() was called recursively, skipped the test files and exited 0, so that run is not valid test evidence. I reran it with that variable removed (env -u NODE_TEST_CONTEXT): both tests passed, output showed tests 2, pass 2, fail 0, and the command exited 0. This meets expectedTestPassCount 2 and expectedStdoutMatch "fail 0" in test-execution-plan.json. The original source, oracle, witness contract, conformance and design documents, test sources and test plan were read and left unchanged. These are my own checks, not admitted observations and not independent acceptance.
